data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name ‘Yoḥanan’ which means ‘God is gracious’. The name Joah is a modern variant of this name and is popular among Christians due to its biblical connection to the Hebrew Bible and its association with the God of Israel. The name Joah carries the meaning “Jehovah is God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Joah usually hope their child will grow to embody jehovah is god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of God's presence and grace in one's life.
data.etymology: Joah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Jehovah is God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Joah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Joah carries a rich cultural history and is deeply rooted in the Hebrew Bible. In the Christian tradition, it is often associated with the biblical character John the Baptist, who prepared the way for Jesus Christ and was a significant figure in the Jewish community. The name Joah is also used in various Christian communities around the world and has become a beloved and meaningful name for many families.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Joah holds a deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Hebrew name Yoḥanan, which means ‘God is gracious’. This name reminds us of God's unending love, mercy, and grace towards us. It serves as a reminder of the abundant blessings God bestows upon us and encourages us to live our lives in gratitude and love for Him. The name Joah is a constant reminder of the gentle and loving nature of God, and the faith and trust we can place in Him.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Joah means "the Lord is stable" or "the Lord is rest." It symbolizes trust and faith in God's unwavering presence and stability. In times of uncertainty, the name Joah serves as a reminder of the Lord's faithfulness and peace.

biblical_reference.note: Joah is mentioned as a recorder in the court of King David

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament, the prophet Joah is mentioned as the son and successor of Jeroboam II, who reigned over Israel from about 782-746 BC. Joah continued his father's religious reforms, but was then accused of idolatry and was imprisoned by the priests of the golden calves at Bethel.

The New Testament mentions a man named Joah (or Jode) who was a disciple of Jesus and a Levite, likely from Galilee. He is mentioned in the Gospel of Matthew (10:3) as one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus to spread the word of God.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Joah, a modern variant of the biblical name Joseph, is gaining popularity in various contexts. It is seen as a unique yet meaningful name, carrying the historical significance of the original name. In the context of social media, Joah is used as a username or handle, often by individuals who want to express their religious or spiritual identity. In baby naming websites, Joah is listed among the trending names for babies, reflecting the trend toward giving children unique and meaningful names. In the music industry, Joah can be found in song titles or as a stage name, reflecting the trend of using biblical or historical names as artistic expressions.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Elizabeth Joah in Rome, Italy credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Joah, which means "Jehovah is God". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
